Why don't birds get fried on power lines? 🐦⚡

Current only flows when there's a voltage difference. A bird's two feet grip the same wire at almost the same voltage, so almost nothing flows through it. Touch two wires at once, though...

#physics #electricity #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why are airplane windows round? ✈️

Early jets had square windows — and the sharp corners concentrated stress until they cracked in flight. Rounded corners spread the stress out. Engineers learned this the hard way with the de Havilland Comet.

#engineering #aviation #planes #learnontiktok #edutainment

Your phone's GPS needs Einstein. 🛰️

Clocks on GPS satellites tick faster than clocks on the ground — gravity and speed combined add about 38 microseconds a day. Ignore relativity and your location drifts roughly 10 km every day.

#physics #space #gps #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

The Sahara used to be green — with lakes, grass, and hippos. 🌿

About 6,000 years ago a slow wobble in Earth's orbit pulled the monsoon rains north and the desert bloomed. The wobble will swing back... in a few thousand years.

#geography #earth #sahara #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Steel sinks — so how do steel ships float? 🚢

A ship is mostly air. Its hull pushes aside more water-weight than the whole ship weighs, so it floats. Archimedes figured this out over 2,000 years ago.

#physics #science #ships #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why did this bridge start dancing? 🌉

When London's Millennium Bridge opened, the crowd's footsteps synced with its tiny sway and amplified it into a wobble. They closed it after two days. It's called synchronous lateral excitation.

#engineering #physics #bridges #learnontiktok #edutainment

You see lightning, then hear thunder seconds later. Why? ⚡

Light is basically instant; sound only travels ~343 m/s. Count the seconds from flash to bang and divide by 3 — that's how many kilometres away the strike is.

#physics #weather #lightning #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Spaceships don't burn up from friction. 🚀

At ~7.8 km/s a returning capsule slams into the air faster than it can move aside, compressing it into a shock layer thousands of degrees hot. The heat comes from squeezing the air, not rubbing it.

#space #physics #reentry #spacecraft #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

There's a 660-tonne ball hanging inside this skyscraper. 🏢

It's a tuned mass damper. The wind sways the tower; the giant sphere swings the opposite way, tuned to the building's own rhythm, and cancels the wobble.

#engineering #architecture #skyscraper #physics #learnontiktok #edutainment

Ice should sink — but it floats. ❄️

Water expands when it freezes into an open lattice, so ice is only ~92% as dense as water (just the tip of the iceberg shows). That floating cap insulates lakes so fish survive winter.

#chemistry #physics #water #ice #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

The loneliest place on Earth — where the nearest people are in space. 🛰️

At Point Nemo the closest land is ~2,688 km away. But the ISS orbits just ~400 km up, so when it passes over, the nearest humans are the astronauts overhead. It's also the 'spacecraft cemetery.'

#geography #ocean #space #iss #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why does the Moon always show us the same face? 🌕

It's tidally locked — it spins exactly once for every lap around Earth (~27.3 days), so one side stays pointed at us. And the 'dark side' isn't dark; it gets the same sunlight. It's just the far side.

#space #astronomy #moon #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

You can't fold paper to the Moon — but the math says 42. 📄

Each fold doubles the thickness. 0.1 mm doubled 42 times shoots past the Moon. In real life you jam up around 7 folds: the stack becomes thicker than it is wide. That's exponential growth.

#math #science #exponential #paper #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts
